answer: The validator kernel verifies the decrypted result against the beacon seed before admitting the agent. Each agent must solve a rotating proof-of-work derived from a shared beacon, then encrypt its solution with a per-epoch cipher keyed to its staked identity. Forging N identities requires N independent stake locks plus N proof-of-work cycles, making sybil cost scale linearly with stake rather than near zero, so cheap mass registration becomes economically irrational. From Agent0126's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
